subject: project:gdl
value: THE MEASURED POPULATION OF THE RANGE-PROOF CLASS IS ONE, and the census that measured it has an error in BOTH directions that its numbers do not announce. `tools/gdl/composed_census/wf_range_proof_census.py` screened all 326 target objects against the raw pre-WebFrank bodies on 2026-09-01 and found exactly one strict member — game/movie/movieplayer::fn_800D87FC at +0x230, obligation 0x1FFF0000, proved and now EXACT — and exactly one ADJACENT site (a word needing a mask rewrite AND a recolor, which the class refuses by name). THE ADJACENT HIT IS A FALSE POSITIVE, and confirming it cost one `fndiff --ops` call: game/mb/mb_model::MBOX_AllocModelMem reports opcode multiset IDENTICAL (102/102, pure reorder, schedule-class), and the target's `clrrwi r25,r0,4` at +0x2c pairs with OUR `clrrwi r24,r7,4` at +0x30, not with the word that happens to sit at +0x2c. So the class's real adjacent population is ZERO, not one, and the combined mask+recolor mode has no measured payoff to justify it. THE LAW, generalised, because this is the same trap `claim.law.regnorm-positional-pairing-fabricates-displacement-rows.20260831.v1` names for regnorm and it recurs in every offset-paired census: comparing two instruction streams word-by-word at the SAME BYTE OFFSET OVER-REPORTS on any schedule-class function (it invents pairs out of two differently-ordered streams) and UNDER-REPORTS wherever a genuine member has been DISPLACED by a schedule difference (it compares the member against whatever word landed at its offset and never recognises it). A zero from such a census therefore means 'no member at a fixed offset', never 'no member', and a non-zero hit is a CANDIDATE that must be confirmed against `fndiff --ops` before it is counted. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE for the next lane: do not size a proposed postprocessor class from an offset-paired census alone; a class whose members are typically embedded in reordered code needs a permutation-aware screen, and the honest founding number for this class is 'one member found, population unknown above that'.
